episodes.165477: A strong cold front moved through the mid-Atlantic during the early morning hours of February 17, 2022. An unseasonably warm air mass was present ahead of it, and temperatures ahead of the front during the overnight hours remained in the 60s. The front was associated with very strong lift and wind fields. In fact, some locally damaging wind gusts occurred ahead of the front on the afternoon and overnight of the 16th. Along the front, a narrow, low topped line of showers and isolated thunderstorms developed. This line strengthened as it approached the Delaware Valley, and produced several instances of damaging wind near the I-95 corridor. The cold front and convective line would then sweep offshore soon after with seasonably cool weather following.

episodes.165534: Strong, gusty north winds rapidly developed in the wake of a cold front the evening of February 17th and persisted for 2 hours. Winds gusted to 36 knots at Rincon del San Jose. || The winds capsized a 16 foot Jon Boat boat near Port Mansfield in the Laguna Madre. Three people were found drowned, one was found onshore just before Midnight the evening of February 17th and the other 2 were found the morning of February 18th. Three people were also found injured; one of those injured died from their injuries on Tuesday, February 22nd. Another body was recovered along Coastal Kenedy County on Thursday, February 24th. episodes.165590: A cold front passing through the area on February 17th resulted in periods of moderate to heavy rainfall. High water was observed along the roads of several counties in the western WV lowlands. This also led to Middle Island Creek in Tyler County to rise out of its banks in the towns of Little and Middlebourne and inflict minor flooding in fields that reside in close vicinity to the creek. The rain ended overnight into the morning of the 18th once the cold front completed its passage.
episodes.165592: Periods of moderate to heavy rain occurred on February 17th into the 18th in response to a passing cold front. Southeast Ohio took the brunt of precipitation, resulting in 1 to 2 inches of rainfall accumulations. Many state roads in this portion of the state were forced to close due to the deluge of water along the roadways and were closed for over 24 hours. The rain concluded on the 18th as the cold front completed its passage, but flooding issues extended into the next days as many of the mainstem rivers rose out of their banks and inflicted minor flooding in areas adjacent to the river.

episodes.165621: As an upper trough persisted over the island chain, heavy showers developed over the Big Island and Maui on different days.  The precipitation produced small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.165817: Several rounds of heavy rain and thunderstorms moved across the region on the 17th. Two to four inches were common, which resulted in isolated flash flooding and more widespread flooding of rivers. The heavy rain occurred ahead of a cold front as it entered southeast Missouri and southern Illinois from the northwest. Weak waves of low pressure moved northeast along the front. A strong 850 mb jet up to 60 to 70 knots was accompanied by a strong surge of warm moist air through the Mississippi River Valley.

episodes.166136: A southeastward-moving surface cold front across southern Lower MI and northern IN approached northwest OH during the early morning of the 17th. The surface pressure gradient tightened in northwest OH as the cold frontal surface trough interacted with a surface ridge axis that remained anchored near the coast of the Carolinas and Georgia. This tightening surface pressure gradient and apparently relatively-deep mechanical mixing of the boundary layer tapping into stronger flow aloft allowed surface wind to gust up to 58 mph in Huron, OH. An area of rain moved east-northeast across northern OH ahead of the cold front during the morning hours. The region was primed for a flooding event due to a widespread snowpack ranging from 0.5 to 1.0 water equivalent across the area, with 2.0 to 3.0 water equivalent in the snowpack across the snowbelt counties of northeast OH. Warm temperatures in the 50s were effective at melting most of the snowpack before and during the rain event on February 17th, with precipitation amounts of 0.50 to 2.00 across the area, the heaviest of which fell across Stark County where the worst flooding occurred. Many area rivers experienced minor to moderate flooding which was aggravated at times by ice jams.
episodes.166153: A storm system pushed across the region during February 17-18, 2022. Warm air pushed northward into the region along with periods of rainfall before a cold front brought the return of windy and colder weather. A convective line of gusty showers also accompanied the cold frontal passage. Some locations picked up over 1 inch of rainfall which led to minor flooding in a few locations. ||In the wake of the cold front, strong winds affected areas mainly along and south of I-90 with gusts 40 to 55 mph observed, resulted in a few downed trees. Some power outages occurred as a result of the wind, mainly across Ulster County.||The warm and rainy weather ahead of the cold front resulted in some snow melt as well as some ice to break up on area rivers and streams. As the colder weather returned, localized ice jams formed, some of which led to flooding, including in Dolgeville and Canajoharie.
episodes.166282: Heavy rain brought flooding to several rivers in northeast Arkansas in mid February.
episodes.166305: During the evening of February 17th, a cold front and associated squall line pushed through the area knocking down numerous trees and powerlines across North Georgia, with the Rome ASOS measuring a wind gust of 62 MPH.
episodes.166307: Heavy rainfall (1.5 to 2.5 inches) and snowmelt led to the formation of a significant ice jam on the East Branch of the Ausable River at Au Sable Forks, NY during the late morning to early afternoon hours of 18 February, 2022. The jam moved downstream from the upper portions of the watershed in the Town of Jay, first creating high water near the juncture of US Route 9N and Stickney Bridge Road. The jam subsequently shifted downstream, lodging near the confluence of the East and West Branches of the Ausable River at Au Sable Forks. As a result, significant water was impounded behind the jam, severely flooding portions of the town, specifically on the Clinton County side of the river in what is called the Jersey section in the vicinity of Broad Street and Intervale Avenue. Flooding was also observed at the local Tops Supermarket and nearby Riverside Park. The river forecast gage on the East Branch of the Ausable River at Au Sable Forks (ASFN6) crested at 15.19 feet, its third highest crest on record. The jam held in place for approximately 2 to 3 hours before moving downstream, easing the flooding in town. Thereafter, it lodged shortly for a second time just upstream of the other Au Sable Forks gage (AUSN6) where flooding was noted along portions of Route 9N and some property on the south bank owned by Northline Utilities LLC. After a short time, the jam moved further downstream, finally lodging in the vicinity of the Lower Road Bridge near the high school in Clintonville, NY. Subsequent flooding of Dugway and Cassidy Roads on the south bank occurred before water carved a path through the jam and high water concerns eased by mid-afternoon. Post-event coordination with Clinton and Essex County Emergency Management revealed 35 homes and 1 town owned property damaged. Of those, 7 were deemed to have received critical damage, with 2 buildings and 4 apartments condemned.
episodes.166391: A slow moving low pressure system brought unseasonable heavy rainfall to portions of our county warning area; 1.50 to 2 inches of rainfall was noted in eastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania in 24 hours.

episodes.166525: A highly sheared and dynamic storm system produced numerous strong and severe thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours on February 17th. Several supercells developed along a pre-frontal trough, which produced a few tornadoes. Additionally, several rounds of heavy rain produced some flash flooding along and|north of I-20, and strong gradient winds ahead of the front caused scattered tree damage.
episodes.166741: A line of thunderstorms moved east across middle Tennessee and north Alabama during the evening hours of the 17th.  Strong winds with the thunderstorms knocked down a power pole in Jackson County causing a local power outage.
episodes.166770: A deep upper level trough was in place across the central U.S. on this day. This translated down to the surface as well, with strong SW flow in place across much of Ohio Valley. Meanwhile, a cold front, extending from a occluded low pressure system in southeast Canada, was located just ahead of the trough, being pushed eastward with the upper level flow. During the first part of the day on the 17th, this front was located NW of the state, making its way eastward. By the afternoon and evening hours, it began to push into Kentucky, developing a secondary low pressure system. This low continued to gain strength, traversing eastern KY, along with the surface cold front, through the late evening and first part of the overnight.||At 21Z on the 17th, the radar showed rain increasing across eastern KY ahead of this powerful cold front. An intensifying 70 to 80kt 850mb jet was analyzed just ahead of the boundary, which combined with some downslope drying, to produce strong to damaging wind gusts across portions of eastern Kentucky. A wind advisory and high wind warning were in effect for all of eastern Kentucky through the evening and into the first part of the overnight given the conditions. Gradient winds were the culprit for multiple trees down across eastern Kentucky, specifically in Clay, Floyd, Harlan, and Perry counties.||Aside from the intense gradient winds, strong to severe storms also develop along and just ahead of the actual cold front as it moved through. These storms helped to translate the higher winds aloft down to the ground, resulting in multiple reports of wind damage across Powell and Estill Counties. ||The event ended up being centered around wind damage, both gradient and convective, all ending just after the front passed through and exited eastern KY by 6Z on the 18th.
episodes.166786: During the afternoon and evening hours, a southwest to northeast oriented cold front moved southeast through central Kentucky. This caused scattered wind damage, along with minor flooding.
episodes.166896: Showers and storms developed ahead of a cold front. Some storms became severe with damaging winds, and locally heavy rainfall. Winds were strong ahead of the storms and resulted in downed trees across the region. National Weather Service official observing sites recorded wind gusts of 50 to 56 mph through the day, and a site in Bolivar County recorded a wind gust of 58mph. Meridian Key Field recorded a wind gust of 60mph.
episodes.166947: On February 17 and 18th a strong low pressure system tracked through southern Canada and ushered in an unseasonably warm and moist airmass. Temperatures surged into the 50s to low 60s. Steady rainfall accompanied by embedded heavier showers with the cold frontal passage produced about 0.75 inches of precipitation. Wind, high humidity, and rain resulted in significant snowmelt where snow was ripe. Runoff was sufficient to raise area rivers, though most remained in their banks. River rises resulted in ice breakup and minor ice jam flooding on some rivers across central New Hampshire, which continued for several days.  The largest impacts were reported in the Claremont region.
episodes.167118: Strong south winds developed across the South Carolina Piedmont ahead of a cold front during the late evening into the overnight hours. A line of heavy rain showers developed across the northwest part of the Upstate late in the evening and produced damaging wind gusts in Oconee and Pickens Counties. Additionally, the persistent south winds ahead of the front also produced some minor damage in York County.
episodes.167218: Flooding was observed throughout much of Crawford County during the February 17th-19th, 2022 timeframe. This was due to above normal temperatures causing steady melt of a snow pack containing 2 to upwards of 3 of water equivalency up through the daytime hours of the 17th, and rainfall amounts of 1-2 on top of the melting snow. Flooding of French Creek and tributaries was observed, including Cussewago Creek, which was exacerbated by ice jamming throughout the 18th into the 19th.

National Weather Service meteorologists surveyed damage in northeast Shelby County and determined that it was consistent with an EF1 tornado, with maximum winds near 95 mph.  A tornado touched down in the Lake Purdy community near Brook Highland Parkway. The tornado tracked northeast causing minor roof damage to an apartment complex.  Large trees were snapped and uprooted as it croosed Highway 119 near a strip mall and a landscaping company. The tornado continued northeast snapping a large stand of softwoods on the east side of Highway 119. The  Greystone community saw a large numbers of trees uprooted. At least one home had a tree fall on the structure. The tornado was likely at its widest and most intense near this location. The tornado crossed into Jefferson County near Sutherland Place Road.

National Weather Service meteorologists surveyed damage in southeast Jefferson County and determined that it was consistent with an EF1 tornado, with maximum winds near 95 mph. This tornado crossed over from Shelby County into Jefferson County near Southerland Place Drive. It straddled the Jefferson-Shelby County line producing mostly uprooted and snapped trees on the west side of Double Oak Mountain.  Sporadic tree and power line damage was observed along Highway 25 with several homes in the Oak Crossing area receiving minor roof and structural damage. One large tree fell through a manufactured home and destroyed the structure. The tornado began to weaken rapidly as it approached Highway 78.  The tornado crossed into St. Clair County near Moss Avenue.
A building near 3rd Street and Chestnut was damaged in Richmond.  There was also sporadic tree damage in the county as well.

National Weather Service meteorologists surveyed damage in southwest St. Clair County County and determined that it was consistent with an EF0 tornado, with maximum winds near 65 mph. This tornado crossed into St. Clair County from Jefferson County near Moss Avenue. It dissipated soon after it moved into St. Clair County with some limited loss of roofing material to a Warehouse.

The jam held in place for approximately 2 to 3 hours before moving downstream, easing the flooding in this portion of town. Of those, 7 were deemed to have received critical damage, with 2 buildings and 4 apartments condemned.

A significant ice jam formed on the East Branch of the Ausable River at Au Sable Forks, NY during the late morning to early afternoon hours of 18 February, 2022. The jam moved downstream from the upper portions of the watershed in the Town of Jay, first creating high water near the juncture of US Route 9N and Stickney Bridge Road. The jam subsequently shifted downstream, lodging near the confluence of the East and West Branches of the Ausable River at Au Sable Forks. As a result, significant water was impounded behind the jam, severely flooding portions of the town, specifically on the Essex County side of the river in what is called the Jersey section in the vicinity of Broad Street and Intervale Avenue. Flooding was also observed on the Clinton County side at the local Tops Supermarket and nearby Riverside Park shown here. The river forecast gage on the East Branch of the Ausable River at Au Sable Forks (ASFN6) crested at 15.19 feet, its third highest crest on record. The jam held in place for approximately 2 to 3 hours before moving downstream, easing the flooding in town. Post-event coordination with Clinton and Essex County Emergency Management revealed 35 homes and 1 town owned property damaged on the Essex county side. Of those, 7 were deemed to have received critical damage, with 2 buildings and 4 apartments condemned.

Minor to moderate flooding occurred on the Green River. At the Paradise river gage, the river crested at 386.27 feet on the 27th. Flood stage is 380 feet. There was considerable flooding of low-lying woods and fields near the river. Some rural river roads were affected. The river remained above flood stage into March.
Flooding was reported along the Vermilion River near East 1251st Road, northeast of Leonore, due to an ice jam.

In the town of Little, Middle Island Creek rose out of its 14 foot bankfull level on the afternoon of February 18th. After cresting at 14.78 a few hours later the creek returned to its banks. Minor flooding along the fields adjacent to the creek occurred while it was out of its banks.
Minor flooding occurred on the White River. Low-lying rural areas near the river were underwater, affecting a number of county roads. The flooding continued into March.

An ice jam from the East Canada Creek resulted in flooding along portions of Van Buren Street and Dolge Avenue in the Village of Dolgeville. Homeowners had to evacuate from at least 10 homes due to the flooding. One of the residents reported chunks of ice knocking trees down along its path and flooding impacting some garages and basements. Flood waters began to recede later in the evening with crews still working into the overnight hours to get the water flowing back into the channel.

USGS River Gage on the Sugar River at Claremont indicated rapid river level rises from an ice jam on the afternoon of the 18th. Claremont Fire Department confirmed an ice jam which resulted in water backing into backyards of residences on Beauregard Street and Twistback Road.
